description: Data analysis, probability theory, distributions, and statistical inference

measures_of_center.mean: Sum of all values divided by count; sensitive to outliers
measures_of_center.median: Middle value when sorted; resistant to outliers

measures_of_spread.variance: Average squared deviation from mean: σ² = Σ(x - μ)²/N
measures_of_spread.standard_deviation: Square root of variance; σ (population), s (sample)
measures_of_spread.iqr: Interquartile Range: Q3 - Q1; middle 50% of data

probability.basic: P(A) = favorable outcomes / total outcomes; between 0 and 1
probability.addition_rule: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B)
probability.conditional: P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B); probability of A given B occurred

discrete.binomial: n independent Bernoulli trials; P(X=k) = C(n,k) p^k (1-p)^(n-k)
discrete.poisson: Count of events in fixed interval; P(X=k) = λᵏe^(-λ)/k!

continuous.normal: Bell curve; mean = median = mode; 68-95-99.7 rule
continuous.exponential: Time between events in Poisson process

68_95_997_rule.68: 68% of data within 1 standard deviation of mean

hypothesis_testing.null_hypothesis: H₀; no effect or no difference; default assumption
hypothesis_testing.alternative: H₁ or Hₐ; what we're testing for
hypothesis_testing.p_value: Probability of getting results at least as extreme as observed, assuming H₀ is true
hypothesis_testing.significance_level: α = 0.05 typical; reject H₀ if p-value < α
hypothesis_testing.type_2_error: False negative; fail to reject false H₀

confidence_intervals.definition: Range of values likely to contain the true population parameter
confidence_intervals.95_ci: If we repeated sampling 100 times, ~95 intervals would contain the true value

correlation_regression.r_squared: Proportion of variance in Y explained by X
correlation_regression.linear_regression: ŷ = a + bx; b = Σ(x-x̄)(y-ȳ) / Σ(x-x̄)²

common_tests.t_test: Compare means; small samples; unknown population variance
common_tests.z_test: Compare means; large samples or known variance
